buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Additional Terms and conditions 1. Scope of Supply and Contract Period a. The contract shall be for the supply of approximately 2,200 refilled comme rcial LPG cylinders of standard capacity 19.0 Kg each, during the period

commencing from 15.11.2026 to 15.03.2027, as per the actual requirement of Government Medical College Baramulla and its Associated Hospital. b) The estimated quantity of 2,200 cylinders is indicative only and shall not cons titute a guaranteed minimum purchase commitment on the part of the instituti on. The supply shall be made on an as-and-when-required basis, and payment shall be restricted to the actual quantity supplied, received and accepted by th e institution. 2. Type and Source of LPG Cylinders a) The supply shall comprise standard 19 Kg commercial LPG cylinders of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limit ed (HPCL) or Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), as applicable. b) The cylinders shall be duly refilled, sealed and supplied in accordance with th e prescribed commercial LPG standards. The service provider shall ensure that all cylinders are procured/refilled through authorised sources and are accompa nied by valid identification and applicable statutory compliance. 3. Arrangement of Cylinders by the Service Provider a) The successful bidder shall arrange the required LPG cylinders at his own cost and responsibility. The service provider shall not depend upon the institution fo r the provision of empty cylinders for refilling. b) All cylinders required for execution of the contract, including their transportati on, loading, unloading, handling and distribution up to the designated Hospital Store, shall be arranged by the service provider. 4. Phased Supply of Cylinders a) The supply shall be made in phased quantities, ordinarily in lots of approxima tely 200–300 filled LPG cylinders at a time, or as per the actual requireme nt communicated by the institution. b) Subsequent supplies shall be made on demand, ensuring uninterrupted availa bility of LPG cylinders throughout the contract period. The institution shall not be under any obligation to lift the entire estimated quantity in a single consign ment. 5. Maintenance of Reserve Stock a) The successful bidder shall maintain a minimum reserve stock of 50 filled 19 .0 Kg commercial LPG cylinders at all times to meet any emergent or additi onal requirement of the institution. b) The reserve stock shall remain available at the service provider's authorised/a pproved storage premises and shall be readily deployable for immediate suppl y whenever required. c) The reserve stock shall not be stored within the premises of the hospital/instit ution unless a designated storage facility is duly approved and the permitted s torage quantity complies with the applicable statutory provisions and safety re gulations.

d) No additional charges shall be payable for maintaining or deploying the said r eserve stock. 6. Delivery Timeline and Supply on Demand The service provider shall ensure timely delivery of LPG cylinders against the de mand communicated by the designated officer/official of GMC Baramulla. The following delivery timelines shall be adhered to: I. Normal requirement: Delivery shall be made within 24 hours from the time of receipt of the demand. II. Emergency requirement: Delivery shall be made within 04 hours from the time of receipt of the emergency demand, subject to the actual requirement a nd directions of the authorised institutional representative. III. The service provider shall maintain adequate stock, transportation facilities and logistical arrangements to fulfil both routine and emergent requirements t hroughout the contract period. 7. Transportation, Loading, Unloading and Distribution a) The entire responsibility for transportation, loading, unloading, handling and d istribution of filled LPG cylinders up to the designated Hospital Store shall rest with the successful service provider. b) The quoted rates shall be inclusive of all types of carriage, transportation, lab our, loading, unloading and other incidental charges up to the Hospital Store. No additional charges on any account shall be payable by the institution. 8. Deployment of Adequate Manpower a) The service provider shall deploy adequate, trained and experienced manpow er for the proper handling, transportation and distribution of LPG cylinders with in the designated locations of GMC Baramulla and its Associated Hospital. b) The service provider shall provide sufficient delivery personnel along with a d esignated supervisor/coordinator who shall remain responsible for coordinating with the authorised institutional representative. c) The deployed manpower shall carry the cylinders up to the designated Hospit al Store/locations as directed by the institution. The service provider shall ensu re the availability of sufficient manpower throughout the contract period, inclu ding holidays and emergencies, wherever required. 9. Quality and Safety of Cylinders a) All supplied cylinders shall be duly filled to the standard net weight of 19.0 Kg, properly sealed, leak-proof and in good serviceable condition. b) The cylinders shall conform to applicable statutory safety standards and shall have valid testing/inspection status. Any damaged, leaking, underfilled, impro perly sealed or otherwise defective cylinder shall be rejected and replaced im mediately by the service provider at his own cost.

10. Statutory Compliance and Licensing a) The successful bidder shall be solely responsible for compliance with all applic able statutory provisions, including the Gas Cylinders Rules, 2016, LPG Control Order and other relevant safety regulations issued by the competent authoritie s. b) The bidder shall possess and maintain all requisite registrations, licences, aut horisations and permissions, wherever applicable, for the storage, transportati on, handling and supply of LPG cylinders through authorised sources. c) The bidder shall also ensure that all safety precautions are followed by the de ployed personnel during transportation, handling and distribution. 11. Delivery Challan and Documentation Each consignment shall be accompanied by a proper delivery challan indicating: · Serial number and date of delivery challan. · Number of cylinders supplied. · Type and capacity of cylinders (19.0 Kg Commercial). · Source/brand of LPG (BPCL/HPCL/IOCL). · Relevant cylinder identification particulars, wherever applicable. The quantity supplied shall be duly verified and acknowledged by the designated r eceiving official of the institution. 12. Inspection and Verification a)The institution shall reserve the right to inspect and verify the quantity, weigh t, quality, condition, sealing and safety compliance of the supplied LPG cylinders at the time of receipt. b)The acceptance of supply shall be subject to satisfactory inspection and verific ation by the designated committee or authorised officer of GMC Baramulla. c)Any cylinder found defective, leaking, underfilled or otherwise unsuitable shall be rejected and replaced by the service provider immediately without any addi tional financial implication to the institution. 13. Billing and Payment Terms a)The billing process shall be initiated only after successful delivery and satisfac tory inspection of the supplied/refilled LPG cylinders by the designated commit tee or authorised officer of GMC Baramulla. b)Payment shall be released strictly on the basis of the actual number of cylinde rs supplied, received and duly verified by the competent authority, subject to s ubmission of the requisite invoice, delivery challans and other supporting docu ments as per applicable rules. c)Payments shall be released after due verification of quality, quantity and adhe rence to the contractual terms and conditions.

d)No payment shall be admissible for the reserve stock unless the same is actua lly supplied and accepted by the institution. 14. Non-Compliance and Failure to Supply a) In the event of failure on the part of the successful bidder to maintain the stip ulated reserve stock, deploy adequate manpower, adhere to the prescribed de livery timelines or ensure uninterrupted supply and distribution of LPG cylinder s, the institution shall be at liberty to take appropriate action in accordance wit h the applicable GeM General Terms and Conditions (GTC), Special Terms and Conditions (STC) and contractual provisions. 15. Right to Accept or Reject the Bid a) The Tender Inviting Authority reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids, wholly or partially, without assigning any reason thereof, and also reserv es the right to cancel or withdraw the tender at any stage in accordance with the applicable rules and GeM provisions. 16. Failure to Execute the Supply a) In case the successful bidder fails to execute the supply of the required LPG cylinders within the stipulated delivery period or fails to comply with the contr actual terms and conditions, the institution shall have the authority to cancel the supply order/contract or take any other action deemed appropriate under the applicable rules and contractual provisions. 17. Submission of Bids a) Bids shall be submitted through the GeM portal within the stipulated date an d time. Bids received after the prescribed closing date and time shall not be e ntertained. 18. DISPUTE RESOLUTION: In case of any dispute arising out of or in connectio n with this contract, the following dispute resolution mechanism shall apply: · Any dispute or difference arising between the parties in relation to this contract sh all be referred to arbitration under the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliatio n Act, 1996, as amended from time to time. The sole arbitrator shall be appointed by the Principal, Government Medical College Baramulla. · Wherever any undertaking or affidavit is required to be furnished by the contracto r, the same shall be duly attested by a Judicial Magistrate First Class. · The tender is issued subject to the outcome of any writ petition(s) or suit(s), if any , pending before any competent court of law.

19. JURISDICTION OF COURTS: All disputes arising out of this bid will be subject to the jurisdiction of courts of law at B aramulla only. 21. Price Declaration: The bidder shall quote its most competitive price on th e GeM Portal in accordance with the applicable GeM policies. 22. Penalty as per GeM SLA. 23. Verification of Weight of LPG Cylinders. a) The institution shall reserve the right to conduct random checks of the weight of LPG cylinders at the ti me of delivery to verify that each cylinder contains the prescribed net quantity of 19.0 Kg of LPG. b) The service provider shall, at his own cost, bring and make available a suitable, calibrated and functiona l weighing machine at the time of delivery for conducting such random verification. c) Any cylinder found underweight shall be rejected and replaced immediately by the service provider at h is own cost, without any additional financial implication to the institution. . 24 Internal Transportation and Protection of Institutional Property a) For distribution of LPG cylinders to different sections/departments/wards/locations within the institution, the service provider shall arrange and use suitable cylinder-handling carts/trolleys at his own cost. b) The cylinders shall be moved carefully and safely. The service provider shall ensure that no damage is c aused to floor tiles, flooring, walls, fixtures or any other property of the institution during transportation an d distribution. c) Any damage caused to institutional property due to the acts or omissions of the service provider or its d eployed manpower shall be made good by the service provider at his own cost. 25. Provision of Gas Pipes and Regulators The service provider shall provide suitable gas pipes/hoses and regulators wherever required for the safe a nd proper use of the supplied LPG cylinders at designated locations. Such pipes/hoses and regulators shall be of appropriate quality and compatible with the equipment in use, without any additional cost to the inst itution. 26. Supervision and Duties of Deployed Manpower a) The manpower deployed by the service provider for distribution and related activities shall work under t he directions and supervision of the Chairman, College Heating Committee, or an officer authorised by him . b) The deployed manpower shall assist in the distribution of LPG cylinders to the concerned sections/depar tments, collection and processing of indents/demands, and attending to and following up necessary compl aints relating to LPG supply and distribution. c) The service provider shall ensure that the deployed manpower performs the assigned duties promptly a nd maintains proper coordination with the concerned institutional officials. 27. Periodic Inspection of Institutional Areas The manpower deployed by the service provider shall, as directed by the Chairman, College Heating Com mittee, conduct regular inspections of wards, offices, OPD areas, laboratories and other designated locatio ns to identify and report gas leakage/repair complaints, defective connections and unnecessary or avoidab le use of LPG cylinders. Any suspected gas leakage or safety-related issue shall be brought to the notice of the concerned institutional authority immediately. 28. Submission of Monthly Company Rate List

The service provider shall submit to the institution, on a monthly basis, the latest applicable rate list issued by the concerned Oil Marketing Company (BPCL/HPCL/IOCL), as applicable, for the relevant category and c apacity of LPG cylinders. The rate list shall be authentic, current and identifiable with the issuing company and shall be submitted along with the monthly bill or whenever demanded by the institution. . 2. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 25% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 25 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 25 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider
